analysis: The supplied units are BASE-side excerpts (lines 41615-43522) of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json. This is a test fixture of golden vectors covering chat_completions, responses and tool-turn prompts, with expected template_input, token_ids, prompt_contract_id, and block-boundary chain hashes. The patch excerpt, which is truncated, shows the PR adding an additional_context {enable_thinking:false} member to template_input and regenerating token_ids, prompt_token_count and chain hashes. Other changed ranges (e.g. 43739-43746, 44524-44630) lie outside the lines I was given. No executable code, auth, key handling, attestation, encryption or coordinator/provider protocol logic changed in the visible material. Security-relevant observations: (1) The fixture feeds the prompt contract and prefix-cache block-chain hashes. Those hashes are the keys for cross-tenant prefix-cache sharing and the encrypted SSD offload tier (T-041). A change to the template inputs, such as enable_thinking, changes the token stream, so contract identity and chain hashes must change in lockstep. The visible patch regenerates them, but the corresponding Swift/Go implementation was not supplied, so I could not check that prompt_contract_id is bound to the new additional_context input or that the scope/cache-key derivation still separates thinking and non-thinking variants. The base excerpt still shows prompt_contract_id 507d6d7a... on the units I saw, and the 8171fec3... id appears in the patch for a different vector. I could not confirm that contract ids were consistently updated across all vectors, because only part of the diff was visible. (2) Fixtures are test-only data and do not themselves grant trust. This does not touch TB-002, TB-009 or TB-011 controls. I found no concrete regression, but I could not verify the producing code or the full diff, so integration should check that the contract-id and cache-key derivation include additional_context.
